name: ChannelPasswordSpec
source_title: ChannelManager.kt — primary project source for the reported verifyChannelPassword implementation (no canonical ChannelPassword CrySL file was found at the requested URL)
protocol: configureChannelPassword? → observe password-protected channel → supply password to verifyChannelPassword → [verification predicate is true] → joinChannel; false → reject or prompt
important_note: The consulted primary source verifies the reported ChannelManager implementation, not a formal CrySL rule for a declared ChannelPassword type. The required ChannelPassword qualified type is a nominal CrySL-name mapping; its existence and formal protocol are not established. The requested canonical ChannelPassword.crysl URL was attempted but was not found.

events.name: configureChannelPassword
events.condition: Observes local password/key setup and local marking of a channel as protected. It does not establish persistence, peer synchronization, remote enforcement, or cryptographic use of the derived key.

events.name: observePasswordProtected
events.condition: Observes only that local ChatState labels channelTag as password-protected. This observation alone does not prove that a password was set, that a remote channel enforces one, or that a supplied password is valid.

events.name: supplyPasswordToVerifier
api_patterns: private fun verifyChannelPassword(channel: String, password: String): Boolean {
events.condition: Observes invocation of the local verifier. Its authentication predicate is satisfied only when its Boolean result is derived from password-validation logic and is true for the supplied password; a call alone does not satisfy that predicate.

events.name: joinPasswordProtectedChannel
api_patterns: fun joinChannel(channel: String, password: String? = null, myPeerID: String): Boolean {
events.condition: For the relevant locally protected, non-creator, no-local-key path, joining is intended to proceed only after a true verification result. Observing joinChannel does not prove that the precondition held or that another peer admitted the user.

events.condition: The detector predicate is a verifier path returning true without evaluating the channel or password. The consulted verifyChannelPassword implementation has that behavior; seeing return true elsewhere alone does not establish this predicate.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That com.roman.zemzeme.ui.ChannelPassword is a declared, loadable Kotlin or Java type rather than a nominal type required by the CrySL naming convention.
That ChannelPasswordSpec is present in the CROSSINGTUD Crypto-API-Rules corpus; the requested canonical raw source was not found.
That a password-protected channel has remote, distributed, or server-side authentication enforcement.
That deriveChannelKey is called on the password-verification path or that a derived key encrypts channel messages.
That every join succeeds at runtime merely because verifyChannelPassword returns true; surrounding state, creator status, and later execution may affect behavior.
That the finding establishes cryptographic primitive misuse, password-storage weakness, constant-time comparison, or brute-force resistance.
semantic_scope: This detector context concerns local channel-password admission logic in com.roman.zemzeme.ui.ChannelManager.verifyChannelPassword and consumption of its Boolean result by joinChannel. It is not evidence of an independently sourced ChannelPassword API or of behavior outside the observed local code path.

detector_semantics.claim: A verifier used as a gate for a locally password-protected channel should distinguish valid from invalid passwords. The consulted implementation accepts every verifier invocation because verifyChannelPassword returns true without inspecting either parameter.
predicates: A local channel is considered password-protected when state.getPasswordProtectedChannelsValue().contains(channelTag) is true.
A supplied non-null password reaches verifyChannelPassword(channelTag, password) on the relevant join path.
verifyChannelPassword performs no channel- or password-dependent validation before return true.
The join caller treats a false verifier result as a reason to return false before adding the channel.
limitations: This is source-level control-flow evidence for the consulted main-branch file, not a test of an installed APK or a particular release.
It does not establish how password-protected-channel state is created, persisted, synchronized, or trusted.
It does not prove admission by another participant, message decryption, or disclosure of channel content.
No canonical ChannelPassword CrySL rule was found, so no formal CrySL ORDER, CONSTRAINTS, REQUIRES, or ENSURES clause can be attributed to ChannelPasswordSpec.

documented_behavior: No standalone documentation or canonical CrySL source for an API type named ChannelPassword was found.
The consulted ChannelManager source handles channel creation, joining, leaving, and encryption-related local state.

The relevant join path invokes verifyChannelPassword for locally password-protected channels lacking a local key, while setChannelPassword derives and stores a local AES key and marks the channel protected.
preconditions: For the relevant join path, the channel is locally listed as password-protected.
The caller is not treated as the channel creator.
No local channel key is present.
A non-null supplied password is available; otherwise the code requests a password prompt and returns false.
unknowns: The intended password-verification algorithm and comparison source.
Whether the password or a password commitment/hash is persisted or exchanged with peers.
Whether any remote participant independently verifies membership credentials.
Whether setChannelPassword is reachable for all channels and whether its derived key is used by an active send path.
Whether the nominal ChannelPassword type exists in another source revision, generated source set, or dependency.

security_semantics.detector_claim: A verification method used as a local gate for a password-protected channel must not accept every candidate password. The consulted method returns true without inspecting either argument.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: If the consulted implementation executes the non-creator/no-local-key password-protected join path with a supplied password, verifyChannelPassword returns true and the immediate verifier check does not reject that password.

source_level: A canonical ChannelPassword.crysl file, or another primary specification source, declaring a SPEC for a fully qualified type whose simple name is ChannelPassword.
A source declaration, generated-source record, or dependency metadata proving the actual fully qualified ChannelPassword type.
Source defining the intended verifier predicate, such as password-hash/commitment retrieval, key derivation and comparison, or authenticated challenge-response.
runtime: A reproducible incorrect-password test for a password-protected channel showing whether join/admission is rejected.
Evidence from the exact transport or peer implementation showing whether membership is independently enforced beyond local UI state.
compatibility: Repository revision or release-artifact identity matching the analyzed source.
Evidence that source, generated bytecode, and shipped APK contain the same verifyChannelPassword implementation.
Evidence that any actual ChannelPassword API implementation is compatible with the detector's assumed event model.

known_false_positive_shapes: The finding is for a stale source snapshot while the built artifact or analyzed revision has a different verifier.
The method is an intentional development-only stub that is unreachable from production password-protected-channel admission paths.
Authentication is independently enforced by a remote peer or transport and the local Boolean is not an authorization decision.
The channel is only locally labelled password-protected and has no security-sensitive admission semantics.
A verifier is injected, overridden, transformed, or guarded elsewhere in the actual build, so the displayed method body is not the runtime implementation.
unknowns: Why the detector/spec identifier is ChannelPasswordSpec when the reported implementation type is com.roman.zemzeme.ui.ChannelManager.
The true fully qualified type governed by a formal ChannelPasswordSpec, if one exists.
Whether a ChannelPassword.crysl rule existed on another branch, tag, ruleset, or non-public corpus.
The intended credential representation and validation semantics for a channel password.
Whether current releases retain the unconditional return shown in the consulted main-branch source.

detector_examples.message: expecting password-protected channels to verify the supplied password but verifyChannelPassword unconditionally returns true.
